subject: science

paperFacts.what: Unit 7 Practical Skills Booklet B ('Practical Theory' on the timetables): three separate 30-minute written papers (Biology, Chemistry, Physics), each 35 marks at both tiers, sat straight after the corresponding Unit 2 paper (10.45-11.15), Summer only; all Unit 7 components at the same tier. Every question is set in a practical context and one question per paper is the 6-mark QWC.
paperFacts.source: research 03 §2 and §5.7; Summer 2025 U7 Physics Booklet B paper front page (docs/sources/papers/science/2025-Summer/U7-H-Physics-BkB-Paper-66897.txt); packs/science/exam-true/tariffs.json U7-BkB (41 papers 2019-2026; Foundation totals confirmed 35 in 18 of 19 parsed papers)

skillIds: Unit 7 skill ids from data/spec/double-award-science-topics.json (U7.<area>.<n>): 1 = planning, 2 = carrying out, 3 = analysing, 4 = conclusions.

corpusCommandWords.note: Command words tagged on the 160 Booklet B questions in data/papers/questions-index.json (counts only)

itemTypes.title: Name the apparatus or measuring instrument
itemTypes.asked: Name the instrument for a measurement or the item in a diagram (gas syringe, conical flask, delivery tube, gas jar, coverslip, eyepiece lens, measuring cylinder, balance, protractor).
itemTypes.examinerEvidence: Apparatus misnamed or misspelt ('gas syringe', 'conical flask'); coverslip and eyepiece lens not named; measuring instruments for density not given.
itemTypes.source: research 03 §7.2-7.4 (Booklet B Summer 2025); Booklet B Physics H 2025 Q1(a)

itemTypes.title: Draw a labelled 2-D apparatus diagram
itemTypes.asked: Draw the set-up in section (2-D), labelled, with no blocked tubes, no 3-D perspective and no four-legged tripods.
itemTypes.examinerEvidence: Widespread difficulty drawing apparatus (C2 F 2025); 3-D drawings and blocked delivery tubes not credited.

itemTypes.title: Identify independent, dependent and control variables
itemTypes.asked: Name the variable changed, the one measured and those kept the same.
itemTypes.examinerEvidence: Control variable in the resistance-length experiment given as the independent variable (length).

itemTypes.title: State a hypothesis
itemTypes.asked: A testable prediction with a scientific reason.

itemTypes.title: Give a safety precaution with its reason
itemTypes.asked: A specific precaution matched to the hazard (safety screen, fume cupboard for toxic gases, tongs, small piece of metal, goggles).
itemTypes.examinerEvidence: Safety-screen wording; where to carry out an electrolysis that produces a toxic gas (fume cupboard).
itemTypes.source: research 03 §7.3 (Unit 7 Chemistry Booklet B Summer 2025); Summer 2025 C1 H MS Q1(c)

itemTypes.title: Design or complete a results table
itemTypes.asked: Column headings with units (matching the axis labels), repeats and a mean column where appropriate; total or mean values computed correctly.
itemTypes.examinerEvidence: Units omitted from headings; total gas volume read by summing table values.
itemTypes.source: research 03 §7.3, §7.4 (Booklet A/B Physics and Chemistry Summer 2025)

itemTypes.title: Plot a graph with a best-fit line or curve
itemTypes.asked: Sensible scale using at least half the grid, labelled axes with units, accurate points, and a best-fit straight line or smooth curve (never point-to-point segments).
itemTypes.markBreakdown: scale [1], labels and units [1], points [2], best-fit line [1] (Booklet B Physics H Summer 2025 Q3(a))
itemTypes.examinerEvidence: Straight-line segments instead of a curve; x-axis label omitted; unit missing from the axis label.
itemTypes.source: Summer 2025 U7 Physics Booklet B MS Q3(a) (docs/sources/papers/science/2025-Summer/U7-H-Physics-BkB-MS-67248.txt); research 03 §7.3-7.4

itemTypes.title: Find the gradient of a graph with its unit
itemTypes.asked: Gradient = rise/run from points on the line (not table values), with the unit of the gradient stated.
itemTypes.markBreakdown: meaning of gradient [1], correct substitution [1], answer [1], unit [1]
itemTypes.source: Summer 2025 U7 Physics Booklet B MS Q3(b); research 03 §7.4

itemTypes.title: Read a value from a graph or extrapolate
itemTypes.asked: Read off with construction lines; state the value with unit.

itemTypes.title: Identify an anomalous result and say what to do with it
itemTypes.asked: Circle/identify the point off the trend; repeat it or exclude it from the mean.

itemTypes.title: Describe a trend using values from the data
itemTypes.asked: Direction of change with numbers quoted; note where the trend changes or levels off.
itemTypes.examinerEvidence: Trend descriptions not taken from the graph (B1 H 2025); potato/glucose flask trend.

itemTypes.title: Calculate a mean, percentage, moles, density or other derived value
itemTypes.asked: Equation line, substitution with converted units, answer to the stated decimal places, unit.
itemTypes.examinerEvidence: Magnification 100/10 done as a subtraction; density = m × V; mass of water to moles; Mr of hydrated CuSO₄.

itemTypes.title: Explain reliability, accuracy or validity
itemTypes.asked: Reliability: repeat and compare/average; accuracy: closeness to the true value, better instrument or technique; validity: only the independent variable changed (fair test).
itemTypes.examinerEvidence: Reliability confused with accuracy (Booklet B Physics Summer 2025).

itemTypes.title: Suggest an improvement or a further test
itemTypes.asked: A change that increases accuracy or reliability, with why.

itemTypes.title: Draw a conclusion, including proportionality
itemTypes.asked: 'Directly proportional' only for a straight line through the origin; 'related but not proportional' for a curve or a line missing the origin; conclusions must cite the evidence.
itemTypes.examinerEvidence: 'Directly proportional' wording; refraction i-r graph reason (curve / not through origin).
itemTypes.source: research 03 §7.4 (Booklet A and B Physics Summer 2025); spec Prescribed Practical P5

itemTypes.title: Describe a method in order
itemTypes.asked: Ordered steps naming apparatus, what is measured and how, what is controlled and repeated.
itemTypes.examinerEvidence: Displacement method for the volume of an irregular solid missed; heating to dehydrate a hydrate.

itemTypes.title: State an observation or a chemical test result
itemTypes.asked: Fully qualified observations ('colourless solution forms', 'bubbles of gas', 'white powder'); standard tests (limewater milky, squeaky pop, glowing splint relights, bromine water decolourised).
itemTypes.examinerEvidence: Vague observation terms; 'cloudy' not accepted for a colour change; 'exothermic' is a deduction not an observation; lithium + water observations.
itemTypes.source: research 03 §7.3 (Booklet A and B Chemistry Summer 2025)

itemTypes.title: State an equation in words
itemTypes.asked: The defining equation as words (density = mass ÷ volume).
itemTypes.examinerEvidence: Part of the Summer 2025 Physics Booklet B QWC.
itemTypes.source: Summer 2025 U7 Physics Booklet B paper Q1(a)

itemTypes.title: Label or complete a diagram or circuit
itemTypes.asked: Add labels, anode/cathode, ammeter/voltmeter symbols in the correct positions.
itemTypes.examinerEvidence: Ammeter/voltmeter symbols and positions; labelling the anode.

itemTypes.title: Select from options (circle, tick, choose)
itemTypes.asked: One selection; two selections score zero.
itemTypes.source: corpus command-word counts (Circle 25, Choose 16, Tick 3); packs/science/exam-true/mark-language.json sci.ms.listing

itemTypes.title: 6-mark QWC set in a practical context
itemTypes.asked: Describe how to carry out or improve an investigation: apparatus, measurements, variables, precautions, processing of results.
itemTypes.examinerEvidence: Fieldwork QWC: few mentioned a key to identify species; some could not name the quadrat.

itemTypes.title: Measurement tolerances (Booklet A carried into B)
itemTypes.asked: Angles to ±1°, masses to 2 d.p., ranges as instructed (e.g. 2.00-2.50 g).
itemTypes.examinerEvidence: Masses to 2 d.p.; mass range 2.00-2.50 g; 25° angle inclusion.
itemTypes.source: research 03 §7.3-7.4 (Booklet A Chemistry and Physics Summer 2025)
